Subject: Forecast taxonomy refresh & 15-min training: Commit / Best Case / Pipeline

Team —

Quick heads-up: we've finalized a small but important change to how we categorize forecast rows (Commit / Best Case / Pipeline). The goal is to reduce ambiguity during weekly commit reviews so our finance forecast aligns more closely with likely closed revenue. This affects next week's forecast cycle.

High-level changes (one-pager attached):
- Commit: now requires one of the following: signed LOI/PO, completed legal review with a named contract owner + explicit scheduling window, or a confirmed exec sponsor + written approval. (This tightens the previous behavioral criteria.)
- Best Case: deals with strong momentum and clearly defined next steps but missing one of the Commit criteria. Use when probability >= 60% and there is active weekly engagement documented in the HubSpot timeline.
- Pipeline: early-stage opportunities, exploratory conversations, or deals lacking agreed next steps.

What I need from each AE:
- Update any deals you currently label as Commit but that lack the new Commit criteria by end-of-day Friday.
- Add a one-line rationale in the HubSpot forecast comment for any move between categories.
- Use the attached commit_review_template.xlsx during Monday's commit meeting.

Quick training: I'll run a focused 15-minute walk-through today at 10:30 AM PT to show examples and mapping rules. Recording and slides will be posted to the Drive. Please join if you own any open deals > $25k. Calendar invite sent.

Why this matters: Finance needs predictability for capacity planning and Dedicated commitments. Small changes here materially improve runway visibility without adding extra processes.

Attachments: forecast_taxonomy_onepager.pdf

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Good question — we are NOT changing probability buckets by region. The numeric bands stay as you listed: Commit = 90%+, Best Case = 60–89%, Pipeline <60%. The main change is that Commit now requires the documented gating criteria (LOI/PO or legal approval or exec sponsor + schedule). That helps account for longer legal cycles in EMEA because a deal can remain Best Case until the gating criteria are met.

What I posted to the Drive (link below) — slides + short recording from today's session, plus a step-by-step page for HubSpot edits. Use the commit_review_template.xlsx for Monday: column headers are Deal ID, Current Stage, New Category, Rationale, Next Step Owner, Next Step Date. Fill that out ahead of the meeting; we will triage high-dollar items first.
